records.name: George Square
records.description: George Square (Scottish Gaelic: Ceàrnag Sheòrais) is the principal civic square in the city of Glasgow, Scotland. It is one of six squares in the city centre, the others being Cathedral Square, St Andrew's Square, St Enoch Square, Royal Exchange Square, and Blythswood Square on Blythswood Hill.

records.name: Gallery of Modern Art, Glasgow
records.description: The Gallery of Modern Art (GoMA) is the main gallery of contemporary art in Glasgow, Scotland.

records.name: Glasgow City Chambers
records.description: The City Chambers or Municipal Buildings in Glasgow, Scotland, has functioned as the headquarters of Glasgow City Council since 1996, and of preceding forms of municipal government in the city since 1889. It is located on the eastern side of the city's George Square.

records.name: The Lighthouse
records.description: The Lighthouse is the renamed, A-listed conversion of the former offices of the Glasgow Herald newspaper. Completed in 1895, it was designed by the architect Charles Rennie Mackintosh.

records.name: Mitchell Library
records.description: The Mitchell Library is a large public library located in the Charing Cross area of Glasgow, Scotland. It is the largest public reference library in Europe, and the centre of Glasgow's public library system.

records.name: Glasgow Royal Concert Hall
records.description: Glasgow Royal Concert Hall is a concert and arts venue located in Glasgow, Scotland. It is owned by Glasgow City Council and operated by Glasgow Life, an agency of Glasgow City Council, which also runs Glasgow's City Halls and Old Fruitmarket venue.

records.name: Theatre Royal
records.description: The Theatre Royal is the oldest theatre in Glasgow and the longest running in Scotland. Located at 282 Hope Street, at the Cowcaddens area, its front door was originally round the corner in Cowcaddens Street.

records.name: King's Theatre
records.description: The King's Theatre is located in Glasgow, Scotland. It was built for Howard & Wyndham Ltd under its chairman Baillie Michael Simons as a sister theatre of their Theatre Royal in the city and was designed by Frank Matcham, opening in 1904.

records.name: Centre for Contemporary Arts
records.description: The Centre for Contemporary Arts (CCA) was an arts centre in Glasgow, Scotland. It was substantially subsidised by Creative Scotland and operated from the former Third Eye Centre in a building purchased in the 1970s by the Scottish Arts Council.

records.name: Glasgow Film Theatre
records.description: The Glasgow Film Theatre (GFT) is an independent cinema in the city centre of Glasgow. It occupies a purpose-built cinema building, first opened in 1939, and now protected as a category B listed building.

records.name: Pavilion Theatre
records.description: The Pavilion Theatre is a theatre in Glasgow located on Renfield Street.

records.name: Buchanan Street
records.description: Buchanan Street is one of the main shopping thoroughfares in Glasgow, Scotland. It forms the central stretch of Glasgow's famous shopping district with a generally more upmarket range of shops than the neighbouring streets: Argyle Street, and Sauchiehall Street.

records.name: St Enoch Centre
records.description: The St. Enoch Centre is an enclosed shopping mall in the centre of Glasgow, Scotland.

records.name: Glasgow Green
records.description: Glasgow Green is a park in the east end of Glasgow, Scotland, on the north bank of the River Clyde. Established in the 15th century, it is the oldest park in the city.

records.name: Doulton Fountain
records.description: Glasgow Green is a park in the east end of Glasgow, Scotland, on the north bank of the River Clyde. Established in the 15th century, it is the oldest park in the city.

records.name: Templeton Building
records.description: Templeton Building is a visitor attraction in Glasgow city centre, Scotland.

records.name: St Andrew's in the Square
records.description: St Andrew's in the Square is an 18th-century category-A-listed former church in Glasgow, Scotland, considered one of the finest classical churches in Scotland, and now Glasgow's Centre for Scottish Culture, promoting Scottish music, song and dance. The church is in St Andrew's Square, near Glasgow Cross and Glasgow Green, on the edge of the City's East End.

records.name: Glasgow Cross
records.description: Glasgow Cross is at the hub of the ancient royal burgh and now city of Glasgow, Scotland, close to its first crossing over the River Clyde. It marks the notional boundary between the city centre and the East End

records.name: Tron Theatre
records.description: The Tron Theatre is located in Glasgow, Scotland. The theatre was formerly known as the Tron Kirk.

records.name: Tron Steeple
records.description: Tron Steeple is a visitor attraction in Glasgow city centre, Scotland.

records.name: Tolbooth Steeple
records.description: Tolbooth Steeple is a visitor attraction in Glasgow city centre, Scotland.

records.name: Barras Market
records.description: The Barras is a major street and indoor weekend market in the East End of Glasgow, Scotland. The term "Barra" is Glaswegian dialect for "barrow" relating to the market's early years where traders sold their wares from handcarts.

records.name: The Briggait
records.description: The Briggait is a category A listed building in Glasgow, Scotland, situated in the Merchant City area on the Bridgegate (A8) and Clyde Street (A814) just north of the River Clyde. Construction of the building was completed in 1873.

records.name: City Halls & Old Fruitmarket
records.description: City Halls & Old Fruitmarket is a visitor attraction in Glasgow city centre, Scotland.

records.name: Merchant Square
records.description: Merchant Square is a visitor attraction in Glasgow city centre, Scotland.

records.name: Sharmanka Kinetic Theatre
records.description: Sharmanka Kinetic Theatre is a visitor attraction in Glasgow city centre, Scotland.

records.name: Trongate 103
records.description: Contemporary arts centre in a converted Edwardian warehouse hosting galleries, artist studios, and performance spaces in the heart of Glasgow's historic Trongate.

records.name: Provand's Lordship
records.description: Provand's Lordship is a medieval historic house museum in Glasgow, Scotland. It is in the Townhead area, at the top of Castle Street within sight of Glasgow Cathedral and next to the St Mungo Museum of Religious Life and Art.

records.name: St Mungo Museum of Religious Life and Art
records.description: The St Mungo Museum of Religious Life and Art is a museum of religion in Glasgow, Scotland. It is the only museum dedicated to religion and art in the British Isles.

records.name: Glasgow Cathedral
records.description: Glasgow Cathedral (Scottish Gaelic: Cathair-eaglais Ghlaschu) is a parish church of the Church of Scotland in Glasgow, Scotland. It was the cathedral church of the Archbishop of Glasgow, and the mother church of the Archdiocese of Glasgow and the province of Glasgow, from the 12th century until the Scottish Reformation in the 16th century.

records.name: The Necropolis
records.description: The Glasgow Necropolis is a Victorian cemetery in Glasgow, Scotland. It is on a low but very prominent hill to the east of Glasgow Cathedral (St Mungo's Cathedral) in an area bordered by the Townhead and Dennistoun districts to the north east of the modern city centre.

records.name: Kelvingrove Art Gallery and Museum
records.description: Kelvingrove Art Gallery and Museum owned by Glasgow City Council is a major art gallery and museum in the Yorkhill area of Glasgow, Scotland, managed by Glasgow Museums. It is located in Kelvingrove Park in the West End of the city.

records.name: Riverside Museum
records.description: The Riverside Museum (replacing the preceding Glasgow Museum of Transport) is a museum in the Partick area of Glasgow, Scotland, housed in a building designed by Zaha Hadid Architects, with its River Clyde frontage at the new Pointhouse Quay. It forms part of the Glasgow Harbour regeneration project.

records.name: Glasgow Science Centre
records.description: Glasgow Science Centre is a visitor attraction located in the Clyde Waterfront Regeneration area on the south bank of the River Clyde in Glasgow, Scotland. Queen Elizabeth II opened Glasgow Science Centre on 5 July 2001.

records.name: OVO Hydro
records.description: The OVO Hydro is a multi-purpose indoor arena located within the Scottish Event Campus in Glasgow.

records.name: SEC Centre
records.description: The SEC Centre (originally known as the Scottish Exhibition and Conference Centre until 2017) is Scotland's largest exhibition centre, located in Glasgow, Scotland. It is one of the three main venues within the Scottish Event Campus.

records.name: Royal Exchange Square
records.description: The Royal Exchange Square is a public square in Glasgow, Scotland. The square lies between Buchanan Street and Queen Street, opening out Queen Street and Ingram Street to the south of George Square.

records.name: National Piping Centre
records.description: Centre and museum in the former Cowcaddens Free Church dedicated to Scotland's piping tradition, with exhibits on Highland bagpipes and other traditional instruments plus an auditorium and teaching spaces.

records.name: Blythswood Square
records.description: Elegant Georgian square laid out in the early 19th century as part of Glasgow's 'Magnificent New Town of Blythswood', framed by grand terraces and long regarded as one of the city's finest urban set pieces.
